invariants.name: Authority Cannot Silently Expand
invariants.rule: Effective authority must be a subset of requested authority intersected with policy authority.

invariants.name: Defensive Decisions Are Monotonic
invariants.rule: Within one immutable run, automated stages may preserve or tighten ALLOW < REVIEW < DENY but may not weaken a prior decision.

invariants.name: No Self-Certification
invariants.rule: The component proposing a mitigation cannot be the sole authority declaring that mitigation verified.

invariants.name: Provenance Before Interpretation
invariants.rule: Unverified evidence may be inspected but cannot become load-bearing trusted evidence without required provenance.

invariants.name: Evidence Is Data
invariants.rule: Captured hostile evidence must not gain execution authority merely by being ingested, parsed, inspected, or archived.

invariants.name: Replay Failure Is Verification Failure
invariants.rule: For a pinned contract, identical captured bytes, policy, and engine identity must reproduce the same canonical result.

invariants.name: Benign Behaviour Must Survive
invariants.rule: A mitigation is incomplete when it neutralizes the hostile case by unnecessarily breaking required legitimate behaviour.

invariants.name: Unknown Is Not Safe
invariants.rule: UNKNOWN, MALFORMED, UNSUPPORTED, INCOMPLETE, TIMEOUT, and resource failures cannot be promoted to ALLOW or VERIFIED.

invariants.name: Resource Exhaustion Cannot Produce Verification
invariants.rule: Exhausting a configured CPU, memory, recursion, decompression, worker, fixture, time, or evidence budget must fail explicitly.

invariants.name: Optimisation Cannot Reduce the Proof Surface
invariants.rule: Performance work may reduce proof cost but must not weaken assertions, coverage, provenance, isolation, tolerances, determinism, boundaries, or replay.

invariants.name: Parallelism Is Semantically Invisible
invariants.rule: Worker count and completion order may affect performance but must not alter canonical security results.

invariants.name: Model Agreement Is Not Proof
invariants.rule: Model consensus cannot elevate a claim into verified evidence without an independent verification predicate.

invariants.name: Semantic Changes Require New Contract Identity
invariants.rule: Changes to policy meaning, normalization, trust, decision ordering, receipt meaning, invariant semantics, or verification semantics require explicit versioning and new conformance vectors.

invariants.name: No Silent Degradation
invariants.rule: Unavailable required verification mechanisms must produce an explicit incomplete state rather than a weaker silent substitute.

invariants.name: Deception Outward, Truth Inward
invariants.rule: Defensive deception may shape hostile behaviour but must never distort evidence, uncertainty, provenance, or outcomes presented to defenders.

invariants.name: Minimum Necessary Intervention
invariants.rule: For equivalent verified security outcomes, prefer the mitigation that changes the smallest necessary authority, resource, user, service, and time scope.
